 Appearance:

Ms. Ayushi Thakur - Advocate appearing on behalf of Mr.
 Verma - Advocate for appellant.
 Ms. Priti Keshwani - Advocate for respondent No.1.

ORDER This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 06/02/2025 passed by XX Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in MACC No.920/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.18,90,882/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 11/03/2022 to the appellant / claimant - injured with interest @ 6% per annum.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that disability has not been properly assessed by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Appellant / claimant has suffered amputation of left leg below knee and Dr. Ashish Mehrotra has given Permanent Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/226) assessing the disability @ 80%.
His contention is that looking to the nature of injury at least 70% permanent disability should have been assessed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9060 2 MA-5874-2025 2.1
He further submits that nothing has been awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal in the head of Attendant and loss of amenities of life and meager amount has been awarded in the head of conveyance.
Appellant has suffered amputation of left leg below knee and an artificial limb has been attached, therefore, in this head also an amount of Rs.75,000/- is to be added.
On the aforesaid submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as aforesaid.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

sentences.text: In fact, the amount awarded in the head of Pain and Suffering is on higher side, which should have been reduced to Rs.50,000/-.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.

Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.
4.
Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. From perusal of the disability certificate (Ex.-P/269) it reveals that doctor has given 80%
permanent disability and for this Dr. Ashish Mehrotra has been examined, therefore, looking to the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant, at least 70% disability should have been assessed to the proportion of whole body.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9060 3 MA-5874-2025 6.

Since no amount has been awarded in the head of attendant, therefore, looking to the hospitalization period and the nature of injuries, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is added in the head of attendant expenses.
7. The amount of Rs.5,000/- awarded in the head of conveyance is also on lower side, therefore, the same is enhanced from Rs.5,000/- to Rs.20,000/- .
There is a amputation of left left leg below knee and an artificial limb has been implanted, therefore, an mount of Rs.75,000/- towards artificial limb is added.
8. The amount awarded in the head of pain and suffering appears on higher side, therefore, the same is reduced from Rs.75,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
An amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is also added in the head of loss of amenities of life.
The amount awarded in other heads are just and proper needs no interference by this Court.

9. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
70% PD comes to Rs.18,41,616/-
 Permanent Disability: (Rs.8,700/- pm + 40% FP x 12  x Multiplier of 18 = Rs.)
 Medical Expenses: Rs.2,27,354/-
 Attendant Expenses: Rs.30,000/-
 Conveyance Expenses: Rs.20,000/-
 Pain and Suffering: Rs.50,000/-
 Loss of Amenities of Life: Rs.1,00,000/-
 Artificial Limb: Rs.75,000/-

Total Amount: Rs.23,43,970/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.18,90,882/-
 Enhanced Amount. Rs.4,53,088/-

Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.4,53,088/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
10. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
